scenes.label: SAFETY
scenes.heading: The space looks safe. The air inside may not be.
scenes.narration: An enclosed space can look perfectly safe, and still hold no air that you can breathe.

scenes.label: THE RISK
scenes.heading: You cannot see or smell low oxygen
scenes.body: Rusting steel, some cargoes and fresh coatings use up oxygen. Toxic and flammable gases collect in tanks, holds and void spaces.
scenes.narration: Rust, some cargoes and fresh coatings use up oxygen, and toxic gases collect in tanks and void spaces. Your senses will not warn you.

scenes.label: ATMOSPHERE TEST
scenes.heading: Oxygen by volume before entry
scenes.narration: Before anyone enters, test the atmosphere from outside. Oxygen should read 21% by volume, with flammable and toxic gases within your procedure's limits.

scenes.label: BEFORE ENTRY
scenes.heading: No permit, no entry
scenes.narration: Get the entry permit. Isolate and ventilate the space. Test the atmosphere, and keep monitoring it. Post an attendant at the entrance with agreed communications. And have rescue equipment ready.

scenes.label: IF SOMEONE COLLAPSES
scenes.heading: Do not rush in
scenes.body: Raise the alarm. Enter only as a trained rescue team wearing breathing apparatus.
scenes.narration: If someone collapses inside, do not rush in. Raise the alarm, and enter only as a trained rescue team with breathing apparatus.

scenes.label: KEY TAKEAWAY
scenes.heading: No permit, no test, no entry.
scenes.narration: No permit, no test, no entry. Every time.
Follow HeyMariner for practical maritime knowledge.

meta.description: Enclosed spaces on board can hold an atmosphere that cannot support life, with no warning to the senses. The precautions every seafarer must follow before entry: permit, isolation, ventilation, testing, attendant and rescue readiness.
